items.title:
io.evitadb:evita_root 2026.2.7 发布, Evita is a specialized database with easy-to-use API for e-commerce systems. Purpose of this research is
		creating fast and scalable engine that handles all complex tasks that e-commerce systems has to deal with on
		daily basis.

		Evita should operate as a fast secondary lookup / search index used by application frontends. We aim for order
		of magnitude better latency (10x faster or better) for common e-commerce tasks than other solutions based on SQL
		or NoSQL databases on the same hardware specification. Evita should not be used for storing and handling primary
		data, and we don't aim for ACID properties nor data corruption guarantees. Evita "index" must be treated
		as something that could be dropped any time and built up from scratch easily again.

items.title:
io.evitadb:jacoco 2026.2.7 发布, Evita is a specialized database with easy-to-use API for e-commerce systems. Purpose of this research is
		creating fast and scalable engine that handles all complex tasks that e-commerce systems has to deal with on
		daily basis.

		Evita should operate as a fast secondary lookup / search index used by application frontends. We aim for order
		of magnitude better latency (10x faster or better) for common e-commerce tasks than other solutions based on SQL
		or NoSQL databases on the same hardware specification. Evita should not be used for storing and handling primary
		data, and we don't aim for ACID properties nor data corruption guarantees. Evita "index" must be treated
		as something that could be dropped any time and built up from scratch easily again.

    slice 2): an S3BlobStore on AWS SDK for Java v2 (Apache-2.0), selected by
    tesseraql.object-storage.provider: s3 and discovered through the BlobStoreProvider ServiceLoader
    (the PdfEngine idiom). One module covers AWS S3 and every compatible store (Cloudflare R2, Ceph,
    Backblaze B2) via endpoint/region/pathStyle/checksumMode. Apps that do not store blobs in S3
    simply omit this jar, so the AWS SDK stays out of their deployment. Integration tests run against
    Adobe S3Mock (Apache-2.0); MinIO is not used (its server is AGPLv3, ch. 50 decision point 6).

    Phase 21): Thymeleaf-rendered HTML templates with page-oriented CSS and embedded CJK
    fonts, deterministic output, rendered through openhtmltopdf (the engine adopted at the
    ch. 50 license decision, replaceable behind the module's PdfEngine SPI). Apps that never
    print PDFs simply do not install this jar, so its LGPL dependency stays out of their
    deployment; putting it on the classpath is the whole install (ServiceLoader, design
    ch. 28, 47).
